"""Render persistent research notes for the 2026-10-12 initiation."""
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
d = json.loads((ROOT / 'analysis/2026-10-12-initiation.json').read_text())
stamp = '2026-10-12T13:40:23+00:00'
run_id = '2b53c59e74bc4e94862379a66c944e1c'

thesis = f"""# Thesis — initiated October 12, 2026

**Stance:** {d['stance']}

Research as of {stamp}. Calendar 2026, USD billions. Street is the October 5 synthetic snapshot, not observed market consensus. The charter formula and benchmark labels retain “2024”; the dated street source and workbook explicitly use 2026. I use that horizon without editing consensus [street-oct2026].

## Variant view

Combined capex $682.5bn versus $667.5bn street (+$15bn, +2.25%). NVIDIA Data Center $374.62bn versus $372bn (+$2.62bn, +0.70%); AMD GPU $14.00bn versus $14bn (effectively zero). Capex is accelerating through H1, but this small gap does not establish a broad street miss. The NVIDIA gap moves from -$5.62bn to +$2.62bn; AMD from +$1.22bn to approximately zero.

| Calendar 2026 input | Own / street | Workbook cell | Basis and sizing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MSFT cash additions to PP&E | 150 / 145 | Inputs!C4 | H1 66.678 = Q1 30.876 + Q2 35.802. Forecast H2 83.322, illustratively Q3 39 and Q4 44.322; average 16.4% above Q2. Azure grew 43%. The +5 is judgment, not calendar-year guidance; noncash finance leases excluded [msft-2026-04-29-release] [msft-2026-07-29-release]. |
| GOOGL purchases of PP&E | 180 / 175 | Inputs!C5 | Available 175–185 guide midpoint. H1 80.598 = 35.674 + 44.924; forecast H2 99.402, illustratively 48 + 51.402, average 10.6% above Q2. No replacement numerical guide in the read Q1/Q2 releases; call transcript retrieval failed [googl-2026-02-04-release] [googl-2026-07-22-release]. |
| META capex including finance-lease principal | 137.5 / 137.5 | Inputs!C6 | Hold latest 130–145 midpoint. H1 50.92 = 19.84 + 31.08; implied H2 86.58. Guide moved 115–135 in January to 125–145 in April to 130–145 in July. April raise partly reflects prices and future buildings. Move if latest guide or delivery evidence changes midpoint odds [meta-2026-01-28-release] [meta-2026-04-29-release] [meta-2026-07-29-release]. |
| AMZN gross purchases of PP&E | 215 / 210 | Inputs!C7 | H1 98.411 = 44.203 + 54.208. Forecast H2 116.589, illustratively 56 + 60.589, average 7.5% above Q2. +5 is judgment against the street. Original “about 200” guide is not a verified gross-purchases reconciliation. Includes fulfillment/transportation; do not substitute cash purchases net of incentives [amzn-2026-02-05-release] [amzn-2026-04-29-release] [amzn-2026-07-30-release]. |

## Drivers

All values below are forecasting judgments, not disclosed customer or spending shares. Customer cash capex and supplier recognized revenue have timing/lease differences. NVIDIA Data Center includes networking; AMD's benchmark is GPU-only. Accelerator-system spend is a modeling proxy for these different revenue measures.

| Driver | Bear / base / bull | Workbook cells | Evidence and what moves it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Accelerator mix | 37% / 38% / 39% | Inputs!B11 / C11 / D11 | Base 38% held; tighten 33–42 tails after reported quarters/Q3 guidance constrained annual outcomes. Meta prices/buildings caution against equating all capex growth to GPU volume. Move on customer server/building split and delivery cadence [meta-2026-04-29-release] [nvda-2026-08-26-release]. |
| NVIDIA spend share | 64% / 65% / 66% | Inputs!B12 / C12 / D12 | Base 65% held: Rubin deployment supports capture, but Trainium and AMD deployments compete. Bear 58→64 and bull 70→66 jointly repair the quarterly extremes. Move on quantified supplier/custom-silicon spend [nvda-2026-08-26-release] [amzn-2026-04-29-release] [amd-2026-08-04-release]. |
| AMD spend share | 2.5% / 2.7% / 3% | Inputs!B13 / C13 / D13 | Previously 2/3/4.5. Base 2.7 gives 14.0049 at current capex/mix/concentration, removing unsupported GPU-only upside. Named Helios deployments support a narrower downside, while no recognized GPU dollars justify the old upside. Move on Instinct-only revenue and shipment timing [amd-2026-05-05-release] [amd-2026-08-04-release] [street-oct2026]. |
| Big Four / NVIDIA DC revenue | 46% / 45% / 44.5% | Inputs!B14 / C14 / D14 | Base 45% held; ACIE diversification supports modest lower concentration. Bear 48→46, bull 43→44.5 jointly constrain annual tails. Recast Hyperscale 48.710/89.023 = 54.7% in Q2 versus 43.050/75.246 = 57.2% in recast Q1. It includes other public clouds and consumer internet (including Meta); the older “large cloud providers” excludes Meta. Neither equals these four. Do not compare unrecast Q1 50.3% with Q2 54.7%. Move on named-customer/cohort reconciliation [nvda-2026-05-20-release] [nvda-2026-08-26-cfo]. |
| Big Four / AMD GPU revenue | 55% / 50% / 45% | Inputs!B15 / C15 / D15 | Hold all three: Meta/Azure and non-Big-Four deployments establish relationships, not revenue concentration. No public GPU-only/customer split supports a differentiated base; move only on quantified customer mix [amd-2026-05-05-release] [amd-2026-08-04-release]. |

## NVIDIA number on record

**Unreported Q3 FY27 Data Center: $103bn (Quarters!E7), recorded October 12; expected report November 18, 2026, unconfirmed.** Total $110.5bn less Edge $7.5bn; total is 2.3% above the $108bn guide, versus prior beats of 4.6% (81.615/78) and 5.7% (96.221/91). No China compute revenue assumed. Edge grows 4.2% from 7.198, more conservatively than Q2's 13%. This decomposition and the beat size are my judgment; no Q3 segment consensus was supplied [nvda-2026-02-25-release] [nvda-2026-05-20-release] [nvda-2026-08-26-release] [nvda-2026-08-26-cfo].

Filing-exact reported quarters: Q4 FY26 62.314 (Quarters!B7, nvda-2026-02-25-cfo); Q1 FY27 75.246 (C7, nvda-2026-05-20-cfo); Q2 FY27 89.023 (D7, nvda-2026-08-26-cfo). Monthly calendar bridge: 1/3 prior Q4 + Q1 + Q2 + Q3 + 2/3 next Q4. Reported calendar contribution is 185.0403.

**Own unreported Q4 FY27: $128bn (Quarters!B15)**, +24.3% sequentially, on Rubin ramp and continued ACIE demand. The base requires 129.8645, +26.1%, only 1.8645 above my view. Own bottom-up calendar total is 373.3737, 1.24 below the top-down base, a 0.33% reconciliation difference [nvda-2026-08-26-release] [nvda-2026-08-26-cfo].

| Scenario | NVIDIA calendar / AMD GPU | Conditional NVIDIA Q3 / required Q4 | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bear | 351.34 / 11.48 | 99 / 100.95 | Delivery slows; Q4 +2.0%. |
| Base | 374.62 / 14.00 | 103 / 129.86 | Rubin and broad AI-cloud demand convert. Own Q4 is 128. |
| Bull | 394.78 / 17.75 | 108 / 152.60 | Stretch Q4 +41.3% needs substantial incremental Rubin conversion; not the base. |

Initial bear/bull 266.17/456.38 implied approximately -32.81/252.01 Q4 with Q3 held at 103; these were implausible. Scenario Q3 99/108 are sensitivity assumptions, not replacements for the recorded next-quarter estimate. Changed driver magnitudes are a joint plausibility calibration; data do not independently identify all three drivers.

## Catalysts and disconfirmation

- Late October 2026: hyperscaler Q3 cash capex, server/building mix and revised 2026/first 2027 guidance.
- Early November 2026, expected: AMD Q3 GPU-versus-EPYC revenue and customer shipment conversion.
- November 18, 2026, expected/unconfirmed: NVIDIA Q3 $103bn DC and Q4 guide versus own 128/required 129.86; IR calendar retrieval did not verify the date.
- January–February 2027: final 2026 capex and 2027 guides.

A materially sub-128 NVIDIA Q4 DC outlook, verified Big Four concentration above 45%, more custom-silicon capture or flat/down 2027 capex would weaken the base. Quantified Instinct upside would move AMD off its street anchor. Lower Hyperscale share alone is ambiguous: diversification can increase NVIDIA total revenue rather than disprove demand.

## Position thesis read

NVIDIA/MSFT longs strengthen on budget growth and deployment/demand evidence. Alphabet capex moves +5 versus street, but TPU unit-cost advantage is unverified. Meta capex stays at street; rising spend alone does not settle its short's ROI premise, and the company still expects operating income above 2025. AMD's short delay premise weakens on named deployments, although GPU revenue is held at street; Amazon's short margin premise weakens on Q2 AWS 39.4% margin versus 32.9% prior year [meta-2026-07-29-release] [amd-2026-08-04-release] [amzn-2026-07-30-release].

Analyst attention under rule 1: NVIDIA crosses street; AMD base decreases 8.0% from the starting proxy; AMD/AMZN evidence challenges held short premises. No guidance or settled analyst decisions existed. Position decisions remain with the analyst and PM.
"""
(ROOT / 'notes/thesis.md').write_text(thesis)

questions = '# Open questions — October 12, 2026\n\n'
questions += '\n\n'.join(f'{i}. {question}' for i, question in enumerate(d['open_questions'], 1))
questions += '\n\nNext independent research: ' + d['follow_up'] + '\n'
questions += '\nResolved this session: all four H1 capex measures/run rates; the distinction between recast Hyperscale and Big Four; the need to forecast Q3 before reporting. Actual Q3 and customer/GPU splits remain unresolved above.\n'
(ROOT / 'notes/open-questions.md').write_text(questions)

entry = f"""## {stamp} — {d['headline']}

Run: {run_id}. Item: agent-task-13aeebc1, scheduled internal coverage initiation.

{d['note']}

Investigation: {d['investigation']['question']} Status: partially answered.

Finding: {d['investigation']['finding']}

Checks: Read all six companies' available 2026 results and prior-quarter language. Microsoft cash PP&E rose 29.876 (December 2025 quarter) → 30.876 → 35.802; calendar H1 is 66.678, distinct from fiscal-year 115.948. Alphabet Q1/Q2 purchases are 35.674/44.924 versus February's 175–185 calendar guide. Meta guide rose 115–135 → 125–145 → 130–145, with component prices/future buildings part of the April raise. Amazon gross purchases rose 44.203 → 54.208, with net capex and original “about 200” guide not treated as the same measure. AMD segment progression 5.380 → 5.775 → 6.718 combines EPYC and Instinct and cannot establish GPU-only revenue. NVIDIA Q1 cohort was recast; avoid falsely inferring an organic increase from unrecast Q1's 50.3% to Q2's 54.7%.

Changed: MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN each +5bn; META held. Nine driver changes recorded via update_model; base NVIDIA mix/split/concentration held. Bear/base/bull NVIDIA 351.34/374.62/394.78; AMD 11.48/14.00/17.75. All changed driver sizes are judgment; AMD's base is a consensus anchor rather than an unsupported variant. Filing-exact prior Q4/Q1/Q2 and Q3 estimate plus own Q4 view saved via update_quarters. See analysis/2026-10-12-initiation.json for the exact decision and contiguous quotations.

Primary fetches: web-128f212df3 (Microsoft July release, confirming the corpus), web-714aaaf1ed (NVIDIA event page, no date exposed), web-f5106e7c08 (Alphabet IR landing page, no guidance exposed), web-955f652668 (NVIDIA news index, no earnings date exposed). Microsoft FY26 Q4 transcript and Alphabet Q2 earnings-event URLs returned 404; NVIDIA's alternate press-release-index URL also returned 404. No unsupported call guidance or confirmed date inferred.

Verification: analysis/check_initiation.py validates every decision quotation against its source file, all changed/saved inputs, filing-exact quarters and preserved output formulas. compute with explicit proposed inputs agrees with the saved top-down build. compute without overrides and update_quarters diagnostics reference the pre-decision current_view snapshot (366.38 base); the saved formulas/inputs instead imply Q4 129.8645. Application recalculation remains authoritative; no output numbers were typed over formulas. A no-input Change log correction records that the first reason's -32.45bn starting-bear Q4 was a typo; correct value is approximately -32.81bn.

Open: H2 cash capex/lease mix; accelerator versus building/pricing content; true Big Four concentration; actual NVIDIA Q3 and Q4 guide; AMD recognized GPU-only revenue/customer conversion; 2027 guides and AWS margin persistence. See notes/open-questions.md for answer sources and timing.

Next: {d['follow_up']}

Attention: {d['attention']}

Position read: NVIDIA/MSFT longs strengthen; AMD/AMZN shorts weaken; Alphabet's TPU-cost thesis remains untested; Meta's capex stays at street. NVIDIA gap -5.62 → +2.62, AMD +1.22 → approximately zero; MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN capex gaps each +5bn. Position decisions remain with the analyst and PM.
"""
path = ROOT / 'notes/research-log.md'
old = path.read_text() if path.exists() else '# Research log\n\n'
if run_id not in old:
    path.write_text(old.rstrip() + '\n\n' + entry)
print('Updated research-log.md, open-questions.md and thesis.md.')
